summary: More pip examples: requirements files with or without a venv, a custom index URL, offline installs from local packages, a specific pip executable, force reinstall, umask 0022, and running a module inside a venv via ansible_python_interpreter.
questions: How do I install requirements.txt into a virtualenv?
How do I install pip packages offline from a local directory?
How do I use a private PyPI index?
How do I run an Ansible module using a venv's Python?
How do I force reinstall a pip package?

answer_card.title: pip examples (part 2)
answer_card.answer_md:
```yaml
- ansible.builtin.pip: {requirements: /my_app/requirements.txt, virtualenv: /my_app/venv}
- ansible.builtin.pip:
    requirements: /my_app/requirements.txt
    extra_args: -i https://example.com/pypi/simple
- ansible.builtin.pip:
    requirements: /my_app/requirements.txt
    extra_args: "--no-index --find-links=file:///my_downloaded_packages_dir"
- ansible.builtin.pip: {name: bottle, executable: pip3.13}
- ansible.builtin.pip: {name: bottle, state: forcereinstall}
- ansible.builtin.pip: {name: bottle, umask: "0022"}
  become: true
```
To run modules in the venv: `pip` with `virtualenv_command: "{{ ansible_python_interpreter }} -m venv"`, then set `ansible_python_interpreter: <venv>/bin/python` on later tasks (Debian needs the `python*-venv` package).
